en: seonnyeo; heavenly maiden; celestial nymph in folk tales

examples.en: In old tales there is a heavenly maiden who comes down from the sky.
The heavenly maiden lived with the woodcutter.
She wore beautiful clothes like a heavenly maiden.
The kids listened to the story of the heavenly maiden and the woodcutter.
The heavenly maiden in her feather robe rose to the sky.
In the play, I took the role of the heavenly maiden.

explain: '선녀'는 한국 옛이야기 '선녀와 나무꾼'에 나오는 하늘의 여자예요. 서양의 '요정'과 비슷해 보이지만 날개옷을 입고 하늘에서 내려온다는 점이 달라요.

phrases.example: 어릴 때 선녀와 나무꾼 이야기를 많이 들었어요.
phrases.en: When I was little, I often heard the story of the Heavenly Maiden and the Woodcutter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 선녀가 나오는 유명한 한국 옛이야기 제목이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The title of a well-known Korean folktale featuring a seonnyeo.
phrases.en_equiv: The Heavenly Maiden and the Woodcutter

phrases.en: The woodcutter hid the heavenly maiden's winged robe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이야기 속에서 선녀가 하늘로 돌아갈 때 필요한 옷이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: In the tale, this is the robe she needs to return to heaven.

phrases.en: She looked like a heavenly maiden in her hanbok.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아름답고 곱다고 칭찬할 때 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as a comparison to praise someone as beautiful and graceful.

explain_en: 선녀 is the heavenly woman in the Korean folk tale '선녀와 나무꾼'. She resembles a Western fairy (요정), but she comes from heaven wearing a feather robe.

en: to be good-natured; to be good-tempered; to be gentle

examples.en: My aunt has an easygoing, gentle personality.
He's so easygoing that he gets along with anyone.
His clothes and the way he talked were both unpretentious.
The way he smiled so unpretentiously looked comfortable.
The landlord was so easygoing that I felt relieved.

examples.ko: 수더분하지만 할 말은 다 하는 사람이에요.
examples.en: He's easygoing, but he still says what needs to be said.

explain: '털털하다'와 비슷하게 꾸밈없고 까다롭지 않은 사람을 좋게 말할 때 써요. 반대로 까다롭고 예민한 사람은 '까다롭다'나 '예민하다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: My sister has an easygoing personality, so she is popular.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 성격을 설명할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common form for describing personality.

phrases.en: He looks easygoing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이나 첫인상을 말할 때 '보이다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Combined with 보이다 for appearance or first impressions.

phrases.en: That person isn't very easygoing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 까다롭다는 뜻을 부드럽게 돌려 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A gentle way to say someone is picky.

explain_en: Like '털털하다', it describes a person who is unpretentious and not fussy, in a good way. The opposite types are called '까다롭다' (picky) or '예민하다' (sensitive).

t90.ax: My aunt has an easygoing, gentle personality.

en: to quarrel; to be on bad terms; to argue

examples.en: My brother and I bicker every time we meet.
The two who used to squabble ended up getting married.
That couple bickers but makes up quickly.

examples.ko: 작은 일로 아옹다옹하지 말고 사이좋게 지내세요.
examples.en: Don't squabble over little things; get along nicely.

examples.ko: 아옹다옹하면서 정이 든다는 말이 맞는 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think it's true that you grow fond of each other while bickering.
My parents still bicker once in a while.

explain: 부부, 형제, 친구처럼 가까운 사이에서 사소한 일로 티격태격할 때 써요. 부사 '아옹다옹'을 앞에 붙여 '아옹다옹 다투다'라고도 해요. 서로 미워하는 큰 싸움보다는 정이 느껴지는 말다툼이에요.

phrases.en: The two friends bicker whenever they meet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사 '아옹다옹'을 앞에 붙여 쓴 말로, 뜻은 같고 말투가 조금 더 부드러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Puts the adverb 아옹다옹 before 'to quarrel'; same meaning, with a slightly softer tone.

phrases.en: I squabbled with my younger sibling over a small thing.
phrases.nuance_ko: '아옹다옹하다'와 뜻이 비슷하고 일상 대화에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 아옹다옹하다 but more common in everyday speech.

phrases.en: Please don't bicker here.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정 명령형이라서 다투는 사람들에게 그만하라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative command used to tell people to stop bickering.

explain_en: Use it for close people such as spouses, siblings or friends who bicker over small things. You can also say '아옹다옹 다투다' with the adverb. It is a quarrel with affection in it, not a bitter fight.

t90.ax: My parents still bicker once in a while.

en: to be overambitious; to be presumptuous

examples.ko: 저 사람은 웃고 있지만 속은 엉큼해요.
examples.en: That person is smiling, but is sly inside.
You look gentle, but you're surprisingly sly.
Don't slyly eavesdrop on other people's conversations.

examples.ko: 엉큼해 보이는 사람은 조심하는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's better to be careful around people who seem sly.

examples.ko: 그 사람, 알고 보니 꽤 엉큼했어요.
examples.en: As it turned out, that guy was quite devious.
I noticed his sly motive and turned him down.

explain: 겉으로는 모르는 척하면서 속으로 딴생각이나 꿍꿍이를 품은 사람에게 써서 칭찬이 아니에요. '음흉하다'와 비슷하게 쓰이고, 상황에 따라 이성에게 흑심이 있다는 느낌으로 들릴 수 있으니 조심해서 써요.

phrases.example: 그는 엉큼한 생각을 하고 있는 것 같아요.
phrases.en: He seems to be having sly thoughts.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉으로 드러내지 않은 나쁜 속셈을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for hidden, ill-intentioned plans that aren't shown outwardly.

phrases.en: His smile looks a bit sly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습에서 느끼는 인상을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for an impression you get from someone's appearance.

phrases.en: He is sly, so it's hard to trust him.
phrases.nuance_ko: '엉큼하다'와 비슷하지만 더 나쁜 속마음이 있다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '엉큼하다' but suggests an even worse hidden intent.

explain_en: It describes someone who pretends not to know while hiding other thoughts or schemes, so it is never a compliment. It is used much like '음흉하다', and depending on context it can sound like someone has improper romantic intentions, so use it with care.

examples.en: The village women were gathered by the well.

examples.ko: 사극에 나오는 여인네의 옷이 정말 예뻐요.
examples.en: The clothes of the women in historical dramas are really pretty.

examples.ko: 여인네 한 명이 시장에서 나물을 팔고 있었어요.
examples.en: A woman was selling wild greens at the market.
A rumor spread among the women.
That woman walked away with a child on her back.

examples.ko: 할머니가 옛날 여인네들의 삶을 말해 주셨어요.
examples.en: Grandmother told me about the lives of women in the old days.

explain: 약간 옛스럽고 격식 없는 느낌이 있어서 사극, 소설, 옛날이야기에서 자주 만나요. 요즘 말로는 '여자분들'이나 '여성'이라고 하고, 지금 앞에 있는 사람에게 쓰는 건 피하는 게 안전해요.

phrases.en: The women are selling vegetables at the market.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-들'을 붙여 여러 명을 말할 때 써요. 옛이야기 같은 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-들' for several women; it has an old-fashioned storytelling feel.

phrases.example: 드라마 속 옛 여인네의 한복이 아름다워요.
phrases.en: The hanbok of the woman of old in the drama is beautiful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옛날 시대의 여성을 말할 때 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits when talking about women of a past era.

phrases.en: The village women made kimchi together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시골이나 마을의 여성들을 정겹게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A warm way to refer to women of a village.

explain_en: It has a slightly old-fashioned, informal feel, so you often meet it in historical dramas, novels and old tales. In modern speech people say '여자분들' or '여성', and it is safer not to use it for a person right in front of you.

t90.ax: A rumor spread among the women.

examples.ko: 두 배우의 열애 소식에 팬들이 놀랐어요.
examples.en: Fans were surprised by the news of the two actors' romance.

examples.ko: 열애 중인 커플이 공개 데이트를 했어요.
examples.en: The couple in a romance went on a public date.

examples.ko: 그 소설은 십 대들의 열애를 그렸어요.
examples.en: That novel depicts the passionate love of teenagers.

examples.ko: 오 년의 열애 끝에 두 사람은 결혼하기로 했어요.
examples.en: After five years of passionate love, the two decided to marry.

examples.ko: 영화 속 열애 장면이 너무 아름다웠어요.
examples.en: The passionate love scene in the movie was so beautiful.

examples.ko: 열애가 알려지자 가수는 팬들에게 편지를 썼어요.
examples.en: When the romance became known, the singer wrote a letter to the fans.

explain: '연애'보다 불꽃 같은 사랑이라는 느낌이 강하고, 대부분 연예인 기사에서 '열애설', '열애 중'으로 보여요. 일반 사람이 '저 지금 열애 중이에요'라고 하면 약간 장난스럽거나 과장되게 들려요. 보통 대화에서는 '연애하다', '사귀다'를 써요.

phrases.en: The two denied the dating rumors.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연예인 기사에서 가장 자주 나오는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form most common in celebrity news.

phrases.en: That singer is in a hot romance these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 사랑하고 있다는 뜻이고, 일반인에게 쓰면 장난스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means currently in love; it sounds playful for ordinary people.

phrases.en: The actor admitted to the relationship.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연예 뉴스에서 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing often used in entertainment news.

explain_en: It feels more fiery than '연애' and mostly appears in celebrity news as '열애설' or '열애 중'. If an ordinary person says '저 지금 열애 중이에요', it sounds a bit playful or exaggerated. In regular conversation people say '연애하다' or '사귀다'.

examples.en: My son must take after his mother's side, since his eyes are big like hers.
I take after my mother's side, so I'm tall like my maternal uncle.

examples.ko: 아이가 외탁하면 엄마 쪽 가족을 닮아요.
examples.en: When a child takes after the mother's side, they look like her family.

examples.ko: 외탁한 아이들은 다 엄마 쪽 눈매예요.
examples.en: The children who take after their mother's side all have her eyes.
My brother looks like Dad, and I take after Mom's side.
Everyone says I take after my mother's side.

explain: 외가 쪽, 곧 엄마 쪽 가족을 닮았다고 할 때 써요. 아빠 쪽을 닮는 것은 '친탁'이라고 해요. 일상에서는 '엄마 쪽을 닮았다'라고 풀어서 말하는 사람도 많아요.

phrases.en: I take after my mother's side, so my eyes look like my mom's.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 닮은 모습을 말할 때 쓰는 과거형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past form, for a resemblance that already shows.

phrases.example: 외탁한 아이라서 외할머니와 웃는 모습이 같아요.
phrases.en: The child takes after the mother's side, so the smile is like the maternal grandmother's.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ'을 붙여서 아이나 사람을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-n' form is used to describe a child or person.
phrases.en_equiv: a child who takes after the mother's side

phrases.en: I look more like my mom's side than my dad's.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 같고, 풀어서 쉽게 말하는 방법이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, an easier way to say it in plain words.

explain_en: It is used when someone resembles the mother's side of the family. Resembling the father's side is called '친탁'. In daily life many people simply say '엄마 쪽을 닮았다' (looks like Mom's side).

examples.en: I have looked up to my older brother since childhood.
People admired that teacher and followed him.
I lifted my head and looked up at the stars in the sky.
He is an actor everyone looks up to.
If you only look up to someone, your confidence shrinks.
I look up to and respect my parents.

explain: 고개를 들어 위를 보는 뜻도 있고, 훌륭하다고 존경하는 뜻으로도 써요. 반대는 '내려다보다'이고, 낮게 보는 뜻으로는 '깔보다'를 써요. 사람에게 쓸 때는 '~를 우러러보다'로 말해요.

phrases.en: If you look up at the sky at night, there are many stars.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고개를 들어 위를 본다는 원래 뜻으로 쓰인 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the original meaning of looking upward.
phrases.en_equiv: to look up at the sky

phrases.en: That person is someone I look up to.
phrases.nuance_ko: 존경하는 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to refer to someone you respect.

phrases.en: I respect my teacher.
phrases.nuance_ko: '우러러보다'의 존경하는 뜻과 비슷하지만 더 직접적으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Close to the 'respect' sense of '우러러보다' but more direct.

explain_en: It can mean lifting your head to look up, and also to look up to someone with respect. The opposite is '내려다보다', and for looking down on someone you use '깔보다'. For people it is said as '~를 우러러보다'.

t90.ax: He is an actor everyone looks up to.

examples.en: I spent my childhood in the countryside.
My childhood memories are hazy but happy.
In early childhood, kids grow up healthy by playing a lot.
I heard that writer lived abroad in childhood.
I'm still in touch with my childhood friends.
I watched a movie about childhood on the weekend.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '어린 시절'이나 '어릴 때'를 훨씬 많이 쓰고, '유년기'는 글이나 방송에서 나이를 단계로 나눌 때 써요. '유년기, 청소년기, 성인기'처럼 이어서 말해요.

phrases.example: 유년 시절에는 할머니 집에서 자주 놀았어요.
phrases.en: In my childhood I often played at my grandmother's house.
phrases.nuance_ko: '유년기'와 거의 같은 뜻이고 글에서 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same as 유년기; more common in writing.

phrases.en: My childhood memories are still vivid.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어린 시절의 기억을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for memories from early life.

phrases.en: In childhood, the body grows fast.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나이 단계를 설명할 때 '에는'을 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 에는 when explaining life stages.

explain_en: In daily talk people say '어린 시절' or '어릴 때' far more, while '유년기' is used in writing and broadcasts when dividing life into stages. It lines up as '유년기, 청소년기, 성인기'.

t90.ax: I spent my childhood in the countryside.

en: to be double-faced; to be sly; to be double-hearted

examples.ko: 그 사람은 의뭉스러워서 속마음을 알 수 없어요.
examples.en: He is sly, so I can't tell what he really thinks.
The way he smiles so slyly looks a bit suspicious.
My younger sibling came out of the room with a sly look.
He pretends not to know, but he looks sly.
My grandfather is often told that he is crafty.
Stop being sly and tell me honestly.

explain: 속으로는 다 알면서 겉으로는 모르는 척하는 능청스러운 느낌이에요. 칭찬하는 말은 아니고, 속셈이 있어 보인다는 느낌이 들어요. 주로 '의뭉스러운 사람/표정'처럼 써요.

phrases.example: 그는 다 알면서 모르는 척하는 의뭉스러운 사람이에요.
phrases.en: He's a sly person who pretends not to know even though he knows everything.
phrases.nuance_ko: 능청스럽고 속셈이 있어 보이는 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a person who seems sly and has a hidden agenda.

phrases.example: 그는 질문에 대답하지 않고 의뭉스럽게 웃었어요.
phrases.en: He didn't answer the question and just smiled slyly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-게'를 붙여 능청스럽게 행동하는 모습을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-게' it shows acting in a feigned-innocent way.

phrases.en: He's smiling, but somehow he looks sly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 보이다'로 겉모습에서 느껴지는 인상을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-아/어 보이다' it gives the impression one gets from appearances.

explain_en: It gives the feeling of someone who knows everything inside but acts as if they know nothing. It is not a compliment and suggests a hidden agenda. It is mostly used like '의뭉스러운 사람' or '의뭉스러운 표정'.

examples.en: I get along very well with my stepfather.
My stepfather took me to school.
That child calls his stepfather 'Dad'.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 의붓아버지 덕분에 큰 도움을 받았어요.
examples.en: When I was young, I got a lot of help thanks to my stepfather.
My stepfather devotes himself to his new family.
My friend's stepfather is really good at cooking.

explain: 어머니가 재혼해서 생긴 아버지를 말해요. 직접 부를 때는 '의붓아버지'라고 하지 않고 '아버지', '아빠'라고 불러요. 글이나 서류에서는 '계부'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I wrote my stepfather's name on the document.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서류나 글에서 쓰는 격식 있는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal word used in documents and writing.

phrases.en: My stepfather is really good to me.
phrases.nuance_ko: '의붓아버지'보다 부드럽고 일상에서 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Softer than 의붓아버지 and more common in daily speech.

phrases.en: I live with my stepfather.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '와/과'를 붙여 가족 상황을 소개할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with the particle 와/과 to explain one's family situation.

explain_en: It refers to the father you gain when your mother remarries. When addressing him directly, people don't say '의붓아버지' but call him '아버지' or '아빠'. In writing or documents it is also called '계부'.

t90.ax: My stepfather took me to school.

examples.ko: 여행 중에 오랜 친구와 우연히 조우했어요.
examples.en: I ran into an old friend by chance while traveling.

examples.ko: 산길에서 멧돼지와 조우하면 천천히 물러나야 해요.
examples.en: If you come across a wild boar on a mountain path, you should back away slowly.

examples.ko: 연구팀이 희귀한 새와 조우한 순간을 영상으로 남겼어요.
examples.en: The research team recorded on video the moment they encountered a rare bird.

examples.ko: 이 책에서 새로운 생각과 조우하게 될 거예요.
examples.en: In this book, you will come across new ideas.

examples.ko: 운이 좋으면 숲에서 사슴과 조우할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you're lucky, you might encounter a deer in the forest.

examples.ko: 십 년 만에 조우했을 때 서로 얼굴을 못 알아봤어요.
examples.en: When we met again after ten years, we didn't recognize each other's faces.

explain: '만나다'보다 글에서 쓰는 느낌이 강하고, 약속 없이 뜻밖에 마주친다는 느낌이 있어요. 사람뿐 아니라 동물, 생각, 사건과도 써요. 약속해서 만날 때는 '만나다'를 쓰는 게 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I ran into my old teacher by chance at the airport.
phrases.nuance_ko: '우연히'를 붙이면 뜻밖의 만남이라는 느낌이 더 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 우연히 makes the unexpected nature of the meeting clearer.

phrases.example: 여행 중에 놀라운 풍경과 조우하게 됐어요.
phrases.en: During the trip, I came upon an amazing view.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻밖의 만남이 결과로 생겼다는 느낌이에요. 풍경이나 사건에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Suggests the encounter came about unexpectedly; also used for scenery or events.

phrases.example: 두 사람이 조우한 순간 모두 조용해졌어요.
phrases.en: The moment the two met, everyone fell silent.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마주친 바로 그때를 글처럼 표현할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A literary way to describe the very moment of meeting.

explain_en: It feels more like written language than '만나다' (to meet), and carries a sense of unexpectedly running into someone or something. It is used not only for people but also for animals, ideas and events. For planned meetings, '만나다' is more natural.

gh: meet; everyday, any person or place
meet face to face, often confronting

p.n: 만나다 is the everyday word; 조우하다 is literary and implies an unexpected encounter.

t90.ax: In this book, you will come across new ideas.

en: to be stupid; to be thoughtless

examples.ko: 슬픈 장면도 아닌데 눈물이 나서 주책스러워요.
examples.en: It's not even a sad scene, yet I'm tearing up, which is silly of me.

examples.ko: 분위기도 모르고 크게 웃다니 제가 좀 주책스러웠어요.
examples.en: Laughing loudly without reading the mood, I was a bit out of line.

examples.ko: 아버지는 가끔 주책스러운 농담으로 분위기를 깨세요.
examples.en: My father sometimes ruins the mood with tactless jokes.

examples.ko: 오랜만에 만났다고 너무 주책스럽게 굴었나 봐요.
examples.en: I think I acted too foolishly just because we met after a long time.

examples.ko: 제가 주책스러워 보일까 봐 말을 아꼈어요.
examples.en: I held back my words for fear of looking foolish.

examples.ko: 나이 많은 사람이 그러면 주책스럽다고 하는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people say it's inappropriate when an older person does that.

explain: '주책없다', '주책이다'도 비슷하게 쓰고, '주책을 떨다/부리다'처럼 말하기도 해요. 상황이나 나이에 맞지 않게 경솔한 행동을 할 때 쓰고, 자기 행동을 '제가 주책이죠'처럼 겸연쩍게 말할 때도 많아요. 'ㅂ' 불규칙이라 '주책스러워요'가 돼요.

phrases.example: 주책없이 아무 데서나 큰 소리로 노래하면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: You shouldn't sing loudly anywhere without thinking.
phrases.nuance_ko: '주책스럽다'와 비슷하게 상황에 맞지 않게 경솔한 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 주책스럽다: acting thoughtlessly, out of keeping with the situation.

phrases.en: I got drunk and made a fool of myself.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경솔하거나 주제넘은 행동을 할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing used when acting rashly or inappropriately.

phrases.example: 공연 중에 큰 소리로 전화한 건 주책스러운 행동이었어요.
phrases.en: Talking loudly on the phone during the show was thoughtless behavior.
phrases.nuance_ko: '주책스럽다'를 명사 앞에 붙인 모양으로 행동을 평가할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form before a noun, used to judge behavior.

explain_en: '주책없다' and '주책이다' are used similarly, and people also say '주책을 떨다/부리다'. It describes careless behavior that doesn't suit the situation or one's age, and people often say it about themselves sheepishly. It is a ㅂ-irregular, so it becomes '주책스러워요'.

t90.ax: I held back my words for fear of looking foolish.

en: to hug; to hold; to embrace

examples.en: I warmly hugged the friend I hadn't seen in ages.
I cried hugging my family at the airport.
The winning players hugged each other.
After hugging my child, I felt at ease.
The sight of the couple embracing was beautiful.
There are countries where people hug when they greet.

explain: '안다'와 뜻은 비슷하지만 '포옹하다'는 서로 껴안는 장면을 글처럼 말하는 느낌이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '안아 주다', '안기다', '껴안다'가 더 자연스러워요. 뉴스나 소설, 영화 설명에서는 '포옹하다'가 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The two hugged each other without a word.
phrases.nuance_ko: '서로'를 붙이면 둘이 같이 껴안는 장면이 더 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '서로' makes it clear that both people are hugging.

phrases.example: 친구가 따뜻한 포옹으로 저를 위로해 줬어요.
phrases.en: My friend comforted me with a warm hug.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '포옹'과 자주 같이 쓰는 말로, 위로나 반가움을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a common collocation with the noun '포옹', showing comfort or gladness.

phrases.en: I held the child tightly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '포옹하다'보다 일상 대화에서 더 자연스럽고 힘을 주어 안는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This sounds more natural in everyday talk and suggests holding someone tightly.

explain_en: Similar to 안다, but 포옹하다 reads like describing a hugging scene in writing. In daily talk, 안아 주다, 안기다, or 껴안다 is more natural. News, novels, and film descriptions use 포옹하다 often.

dis.h: formal Sino-Korean word; embrace as greeting
gh: hold or carry in one's arms
wrap both arms tightly around someone

p.n: 포옹하다 is more formal and often a greeting or sign of affection; 껴안다 is plain physical hugging.

t90.ax: The winning players hugged each other.

examples.ko: 그 왕은 백성을 괴롭힌 폭군으로 기억돼요.
examples.en: That king is remembered as a tyrant who tormented his people.
Once the tyrant was gone, the country became calm.

examples.ko: 우리 팀장님은 폭군 같아서 다들 무서워해요.
examples.en: Our team leader is like a tyrant, so everyone is afraid of him.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 읽은 동화에 폭군이 나와요.
examples.en: A tyrant appears in a fairy tale I read as a child.
The tyrant's son became king.

examples.ko: 집에서 폭군처럼 굴지 않는 아빠가 되고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to be a dad who doesn't act like a tyrant at home.

explain: 역사나 드라마에서 나쁜 왕을 가리킬 때 자주 쓰고, 일상에서는 무섭게 구는 상사나 부모를 과장해서 '폭군 같다'고 말하기도 해요. '독재자'는 권력을 혼자 쥔 정치 이야기에 쓰고, '폭군'은 난폭하고 잔인한 성격이 더 중심이에요.

phrases.en: Our team leader is sometimes like a tyrant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 무섭게 구는 사람을 과장해서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in daily life to exaggerate about someone who acts harshly.

phrases.en: People suffered in the era ruled by a tyrant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 역사 이야기에서 나쁜 왕의 시대를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in history stories to speak of an evil king's era.
phrases.en_equiv: to be ruled by a tyrant

phrases.example: 그 나라의 독재자는 오래 권력을 쥐었어요.
phrases.en: That country's dictator held power for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '폭군'은 난폭한 성격에, '독재자'는 권력을 독차지한 정치에 중심이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: 폭군 stresses a cruel nature; 독재자 stresses monopolized political power.

explain_en: It is often used for a bad king in history or dramas, and in daily life people exaggerate by saying a scary boss or parent is '폭군 같다'. '독재자' is for politics where one person holds all power, while '폭군' focuses more on a violent, cruel character.
